response.rationale: Both forms denote the same chronic disease involving high blood sugar. Indonesian commonly uses “diabetes,” while Malaysian Malay commonly uses “kencing manis,” though “diabetes” is also widely understood and used in medical or formal contexts.
response.risk_rationale: Malaysian usage varies by register: “diabetes” may be at least as common in clinical and formal contexts.
response.shared_synonym_rationale: “Diabetes” is also ordinary in Malaysia, especially in medical or formal contexts, but “kencing manis” remains a useful Malaysian Malay preference in everyday usage.
